prompt: A bucket was public for an afternoon. Which kind of CloudTrail event says who downloaded the files during that time?
hint: Reading an object is an operation on the data.

choices.text: An Insights event, which CloudTrail raises when downloads spike
choices.why: The lesson's question is answered by the record of each read, which is a data event.

choices.text: The bucket's own access log, which every bucket keeps with no setup
choices.why: S3 server access logging is a setting too, off until switched on; and it is not what this lesson configures.

choices.text: A management event, recorded by default
choices.why: Management events record the policy change, not the downloads.

choices.text: A data event, if it was selected beforehand
choices.why: Right. Data events are chosen per resource, and a trail switched on afterwards records nothing about the days before.

prompt: An account has never had a trail. What can still answer who changed a security group last week?
hint: Ninety days of one kind, with no setup.

choices.text: Nothing: without a trail no call is recorded anywhere
choices.why: Event history records management events with no trail at all.

choices.text: The security group's description field, which AWS updates on each change
choices.why: A description is free text somebody writes.

choices.text: VPC flow logs, which record rule changes
choices.why: Flow logs record traffic, not configuration changes.

choices.text: Event history, which keeps 90 days of management events
choices.why: Right. It exists in every account, one region at a time, with no data events.

prompt: A record carries an `errorCode` of `AccessDenied`. What does that mean?
hint: Refused calls are recorded too.

choices.text: The trail failed to write the record correctly
choices.why: The record is fine; the call it describes was refused.

choices.text: Somebody made the call and was refused
choices.why: Right, and that is often the first sign of a key being tried against things it does not allow.

choices.text: The record itself is hidden from the reader
choices.why: You are reading it; the field describes the call.

choices.text: The call succeeded, but slowly
choices.why: An error code is present only when the call failed.

prompt: Which of these would a CloudTrail trail NOT record? Choose all that apply.
hint: A trail records calls to the AWS API.

choices.text: A query sent to the clinic's database
choices.why: Right. The database keeps its own logs.

choices.text: `PutBucketPolicy` on `clinic-exports`
choices.why: A management event, recorded by default.

choices.text: The contents of an uploaded file
choices.why: Right. A record names the object, never what was in it.

choices.text: A refused `StopLogging`
choices.why: Refused calls are recorded, with their error code.

choices.text: A command typed inside an EC2 instance
choices.why: Right. That is the operating system's log.

prompt: Why does the trail's bucket policy carry an `aws:SourceArn` condition naming the trail?
hint: The writer is a service that works for many accounts.

choices.text: So the service writes there for this trail and not for a trail in someone else's account
choices.why: Right. It is the confused deputy of lesson 13 again.

choices.text: To stop the clinic's own administrators from reading the records the service writes into the bucket
choices.why: The condition limits the service's writing; it says nothing about people reading.

choices.text: So CloudTrail compresses the files
choices.why: Compression has nothing to do with the bucket policy.

choices.text: Because moto refuses a policy without it
choices.why: moto ignores conditions; the reason is AWS's.

prompt: What does `--is-multi-region-trail` buy the clinic?
hint: Lesson 1 counted 38 default networks.

choices.text: A copy of the bucket in every region
choices.why: The records go to one bucket; the flag is about where calls are recorded from.

choices.text: Lower latency for lookups
choices.why: It changes coverage, not speed.

choices.text: Data events in every region, for free
choices.why: Data events are chosen by selectors and billed per event.

choices.text: A record of calls in every region, including the ones nobody watches
choices.why: Right. A resource started in a forgotten region still leaves a record.

prompt: `get-trail-status` says `IsLogging: true` and gives a recent delivery time. What does the lesson say you still have to check?
hint: moto said the same, with an empty bucket.

choices.text: That the trail's name matches the bucket's
choices.why: They happened to match here; it proves nothing about records.

choices.text: That the bucket holds files from today
choices.why: Right. A status that says logging is not evidence that records exist.

choices.text: That log file validation is off, so delivery is faster
choices.why: Validation is what lets you prove the files later; turning it off loses that.

choices.text: That the status was read by an administrator rather than by caio
choices.why: Who reads it changes nothing about what it says.

prompt: What did moto do with the trail the lesson configured?
hint: Look in the bucket.

choices.text: Refused to create it without the bucket policy
choices.why: That is what AWS does; moto creates it either way.

choices.text: Recorded management events and skipped data events
choices.why: It recorded neither; the bucket stayed empty.

choices.text: Wrote every call into the bucket, like AWS
choices.why: The bucket listing was empty.

choices.text: Kept the whole configuration and recorded no events at all
choices.why: Right, and lookup-events answered HTTP 500.

prompt: The flag `--enable-log-file-___` makes CloudTrail write a signed digest file every hour.
hint: The word that ends the flag.

prompt: In which time zone does CloudTrail write `eventTime`?
hint: The clinic is three hours behind it.

choices.text: UTC, always
choices.why: Right. 12:02 in the record was 09:02 in São Paulo.

choices.text: The caller's local time, taken from the user agent
choices.why: The user agent names a program, not a time zone.

choices.text: The time zone set on the trail
choices.why: A trail has no time-zone setting.

choices.text: The region's local time
choices.why: No region's clock is used; every record is in the same zone.

prompt: In the lesson's records, how many objects were served to anonymous callers while the bucket was public?
hint: The fourth column said `served` or not.

prompt: How does CloudTrail identify a caller who signed nothing?
hint: The query filtered on one account value.

choices.text: As the bucket owner, since the bucket served the object
choices.why: The owner is the clinic; the caller is somebody else.

choices.text: By the caller's IP address in `userIdentity.arn`
choices.why: An anonymous caller has no ARN; the address is in `sourceIPAddress`.

choices.text: It does not record unsigned calls
choices.why: It records them as data events when they are selected.

choices.text: With the account `ANONYMOUS_PRINCIPAL` in `userIdentity`
choices.why: Right. That is the value the lesson's query selected on.

prompt: Suppose the trail had no data events. Which question about the afternoon could the records still answer?
hint: The policy change and the reads are different kinds of event.

choices.text: Whether any anonymous caller was refused after the fix
choices.why: That refused read is also a data event.

choices.text: How many patients' rows were in each file
choices.why: No trail records content, with or without data events.

choices.text: Which files left, and to which addresses
choices.why: Those are the GetObject records, which are data events.

choices.text: Who made the bucket public, and when
choices.why: Right. PutBucketPolicy is a management event, recorded by default.

prompt: Put the afternoon's events in the order the trail recorded them.
hint: The timeline figure at the end of the section.
items: caio puts a public bucket policy
an anonymous caller is served the day's export
dani's key tries StopLogging and is refused
the first anonymous address comes back and is refused
trap: Putting dani's attempt first is the slip: it came in the middle of the window.

prompt: caio holds `AdministratorAccess` and an inline policy denying `cloudtrail:StopLogging`. What happened when he called it?
hint: Lesson 6's rule about Deny.

choices.text: It succeeded, since AdministratorAccess allows `*`
choices.why: An explicit Deny beats every Allow.

choices.text: It was refused, and the trail kept logging
choices.why: Right. He could still read the trail's configuration.

choices.text: It was refused, and caio lost all his other permissions
choices.why: The Deny names four calls; everything else stays.

choices.text: moto ignored the Deny, as it ignores conditions
choices.why: moto judges identity policies; it is conditions it ignores.

prompt: Why does the lesson send the trail's records to a separate log-archive account?
hint: Who could empty a bucket in the same account?

choices.text: So the records are kept in a different region
choices.why: Accounts and regions are separate questions.

choices.text: Because a bucket in another account is cheaper
choices.why: Price is not the reason; reach is.

choices.text: So the administrators being recorded have no permission on the records
choices.why: Right. An administrator of production has nothing on the archive's bucket.

choices.text: Because CloudTrail refuses to write into the account it records
choices.why: It writes into the same account happily; that is the weakness.

prompt: A log file was deleted from the trail's bucket on a Tuesday. Which mechanism would show that, and how?
hint: Every hour, a signed list of hashes, chained.

choices.text: The digest files: `validate-logs` reports a file the digest lists and the bucket lacks
choices.why: Right. Each hour's digest names the hash of every file delivered.

choices.text: The trail's status, which changes `IsLogging` to false
choices.why: Deleting a file does not stop logging; the status would look fine.

choices.text: S3 versioning, by refusing the deletion
choices.why: Versioning keeps old versions; it does not refuse a delete, and it is not what the lesson used.

choices.text: The event history, which lists the deleted file
choices.why: Event history shows management events, and deleting an object is a data event.

prompt: Why does the lesson prefer a service control policy over the same Deny on each user?
hint: The next user.

choices.text: Because moto enforces SCPs and not identity policies
choices.why: The reverse: moto judges identity policies and ignores SCPs.

choices.text: Because an SCP grants the permission back to the security team, who then hold it alone
choices.why: An SCP only limits; it grants nothing.

choices.text: Because identity policies cannot contain a Deny
choices.why: They can; caio's did.

choices.text: Because a guardrail on each user is one somebody forgets on the next user
choices.why: Right. Written once on the organisation, it binds every identity of every member account.

prompt: Which calls does the lesson's guardrail deny? Choose all that apply.
hint: Four calls that would blind the trail.

choices.text: `cloudtrail:DeleteTrail`
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: `cloudtrail:GetTrailStatus`
choices.why: Reading the status harms nothing, and caio still could.

choices.text: `cloudtrail:PutEventSelectors`
choices.why: Right. Removing the data selectors blinds the trail to reads.

choices.text: `cloudtrail:DescribeTrails`
choices.why: A read of configuration; caio ran it after the refusal.

choices.text: `cloudtrail:StopLogging`
choices.why: Right.

prompt: In Google Cloud, which audit logs are off by default, except for BigQuery?
hint: The kind that can be enormous.

choices.text: Policy Denied
choices.why: Those record calls a security policy refused; the lesson does not list them as off by default.

choices.text: Admin Activity
choices.why: Always written, and impossible to switch off.

choices.text: Data Access
choices.why: Right. They record reads and writes of user data, and are billed when on.

choices.text: System Event
choices.why: Those record Google's own actions and are written regardless.

prompt: Match each provider's record of configuration changes to its name.
hint: The first row of the table.

prompt: A file was read from an Azure storage account last month. Where would the record of that read be?
hint: Reading a blob is a data-plane operation.

choices.text: In resource logs, if a diagnostic setting was sending them somewhere
choices.why: Right. Without that setting, there is no record of the read.

choices.text: In Microsoft Entra ID's audit log
choices.why: Entra records identity events, not reads of a blob.

choices.text: In the blob's own metadata
choices.why: Metadata describes the blob; it is not a log of who read it.

choices.text: In the subscription's Activity Log, kept 90 days
choices.why: The Activity Log records control-plane operations, not reads of data.

prompt: The clinic opens a trail today, with data events on `clinic-records`. A breach is suspected from three weeks ago. What can the new trail tell you about those reads?
hint: Nobody can switch it on retroactively.

choices.text: Everything, since CloudTrail backfills 90 days when a trail is created
choices.why: Event history holds 90 days of management events, never data events.

choices.text: Nothing about them
choices.why: Right. Data events exist only from the moment they were selected.

choices.text: The reads, without the callers' addresses
choices.why: There are no records of those reads at all.

choices.text: The reads, if the bucket was in sa-east-1
choices.why: The region changes nothing here.

prompt: A refused call carries the field `___` in its record, such as `AccessDenied`.
hint: The field the last query of the reading section selected on.
